 3 districts on red alert, 7 on orange warning on Sunday 
 Trending Maharashtra Doctor Assault Yamuna Toxic Foam Diljit Dosanjh Himanshu Bhau Manipur Protest Delhi Student Death Maharashtra Doctor Assault Yamuna Toxic Foam Diljit Dosanjh Himanshu Bhau Manipur Protest Delhi Student Death Maharashtra Doctor Assault Yamuna Toxic Foam Diljit Dosanjh Himanshu Bhau Manipur Protest Delhi Student Death 3 districts on red alert, 7 on orange warning on Sunday 
 TNN / Oct 25, 2026, 00:09 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Kochi: Keralam is expected to receive heavy to extreme rain on Sunday and Monday due to an intensifying low-pressure system, persisting over Bay of Bengal, strengthening into a severe and deep depression by Sunday. It could develop into a cyclone over the central-west Bay of Bengal by Monday morning. India meteorological department ( IMD ) has issued a red alert (above 20cm rainfall in 24 hours) for Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad on Sunday. Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad and Kannur have been issued an orange warning (12-20cm rain in 24 hours) and yellow warning (7-11cm in 24 hours) for the remaining districts. IMD said extreme rainfall is very likely at one or two places in these districts. On Monday, Idukki and Palakkad will be on red alert, Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Thrissur and Malappuram will be on orange alert, and there will be a yellow warning for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Alappuzha, Kozhikode and Wayanad. This is the first time a red alert has been issued in the state in this year’s Northeast monsoon. Wayanad, which recorded a 53% deficiency during the Southwest monsoon, has reported excess rain in the Northeast monsoon so far. As IMD issued a red alert, Wayanad collector V Chelsasini, who is also the chairperson of District Disaster Management Authority, has declared a holiday for religious study classes, tuition centres and special classes in the district on Sunday. The collector said strict action would be taken against institutions that violate the order under Section 51(b) of Disaster Management Act, 2005. The collector has also issued an order imposing a complete ban on the functioning of resorts, homestays, tourist centres, including adventure tourism and trekking, in disaster-prone areas on Sunday. The secretaries of local self-govt institutions concerned should take necessary measures to relocate people in disaster-prone areas to safe locations. Meppadi panchayat secretary and Vellarimala village officer should jointly take necessary measures to relocate those living in the Anakkampoyil-Kalladi tunnel road construction area. Kozhikode and Malappuram district administrations have also declared a holiday for religious study classes, tuition centres and special classes on Sunday. The cyclone, as it gains strength while continuing west–northwest, is likely to reach central-west Bay of Bengal near Andhra Pradesh coast by Wednesday morning.
